key_insight: CTLink connects written radiology findings to their locations in 3D chest CT scans. It uses text prompts to segment the abnormalities described in a report.
problem_solved: Radiology reports describe abnormalities in words but typically do not mark them on the scan, making it difficult to match each finding to the corresponding anatomy.
method: Use report finding text as a prompt for a 3D chest CT segmentation model.
Train on 4,123 noncontrast chest CT scans with 9,547 segmented report findings.
Include ReXGroundingCTv2, a newly annotated dataset containing 1,134 scans and 1,895 findings.
impact: CTLink offers a way to ground clinical language in volumetric medical images, supporting more interpretable report-to-image interfaces. The supplied abstract is truncated, so performance and clinical validation cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Pipeline: report finding → text-prompted CTLink model → highlighted region in a 3D CT scan.
Paired view of a report sentence and its corresponding segmentation overlay.
Dataset cards showing 4,123 scans and 9,547 segmented findings, with a separate ReXGroundingCTv2 annotation card.
Chest CT slice stack illustrating how a segmented finding extends across three dimensions.
paper_title: CTLink: A Text-Prompted Segmentation Model for Linking Radiology Report Findings to 3D Chest CT Scans
paper_authors: Mohammed Baharoon, Sung Eun Kim, Mahmoud Hussain Alabbad, Lucas Bijnens, Ali Piracha
